rows.name: lib/bake_harness.py
rows.what_it_does: Turns any recipe into flat colour, height, roughness, metallic and normal pictures by photographing a square from straight above.
rows.evidence: Ran today (look check); the slate layers and the brick reuse were baked through it. Slate layers at 1254 dots: about 3 minutes for colour, height and roughness.

rows.name: lib/recipe_tools.py
rows.what_it_does: Small helpers to add and link nodes and make node groups, plus seamless noise and seamless cells.
rows.evidence: Every shared layer sits on it; build check today.

rows.name: lib/texture_compare.py (+ its anchors file)
rows.what_it_does: The "same kind of surface?" score and its four groups, with a side-by-side sheet.
rows.evidence: Re-scored the five first new tiles today: identical to the stored numbers.
rows.wood: as is. The old wood new tiles were tuned on it, so their score is optimistic
rows.mud: as is, but weak on mud: also score against the other five references as a control
rows.gravel: as is. Quote the as-baked number

rows.name: lib/pixel_compare.py
rows.what_it_does: The "same picture, dot for dot?" measures and tiers.
rows.evidence: Every made-up tile of all six builds is tier "none" (final reports), by design.
rows.brick: as is, only to show a new tile is not a copy

rows.name: lib/description_audit.py
rows.what_it_does: Checks that a description file is a short list of numbers, not a picture in disguise.
rows.evidence: Reading: a layered recipe has no description, only a settings file of plain numbers and colours (slate's is 1.7 KB). Not run today.
rows.brick: as is, on the trial's settings file

rows.name: lib/sweep_tools.py + lib/make_strip.py
rows.what_it_does: Bakes small squares of one setting at several values and joins them into a labelled strip.
rows.evidence: Reading only (35 + 31 lines): it needs a group with a Vector input, which every layered recipe has. Not run today.
rows.brick: as is, with a one-line function that builds the trial recipe with one setting changed

rows.name: builder.py
rows.what_it_does: "Write nodes like a list of sums": add, multiply, map range, ramps, seamless noise and cells, a brick-grid helper.
rows.evidence: The layer helper is built on it; build check today.

rows.name: stone_tools.py
rows.what_it_does: Seamless random stones: one faceted polygon stone per grid cell (`polygon_stones`) or Voronoi stones (`stone_layer`), with mask, facet brightness and random numbers.
rows.evidence: Build check today: builds inside an empty layout box made by the layer helper (166 nodes); the outputs it gives are listed in section 3.
rows.mud: as is, inside a new STONES layer (mask and facet brightness are enough)
rows.gravel: needs code changes: a copy that also returns each stone's centre coordinates and size, so a LAYOUT can make `local_x`, `local_y` and piece sizes

rows.name: hp_tools.py
rows.what_it_does: Painted-look helpers: streaky seamless noise and cells, warped coordinates, palette ramps, padded photographs, a periodicity check.
rows.evidence: Reading only; not run today.
rows.brick: as is, building blocks for GRIME (streaky soot)
rows.wood: as is, building blocks if a CRACKS or GRAIN layer is written
rows.metal: as is, streaky noise if MOSS drips are not enough for rust streaks
rows.mud: as is, warp and streaky noise inside RUTS
rows.gravel: as is, inside GRIME for the soil

rows.name: layout_tools.py
rows.what_it_does: A Geometry Nodes group that places one point per brick, slate, plank or plate on a wrapping tile.
rows.evidence: The layers need eleven numbers for every dot, not a cloud of points.

rows.name: relax_tools.py
rows.what_it_does: A Geometry Nodes group that pushes overlapping points apart on a wrapping tile.
rows.evidence: Only for a real-geometry route; on gravel that route lowered the same-kind score from 0.362 to 0.173 (gravel final report, "geometry_route").

rows.name: gn_tools.py
rows.what_it_does: Helpers to build Geometry Nodes groups and photograph real geometry from above.
rows.evidence: The layered route is shader nodes only; all six builds found real geometry did not help when the reference maps were made from the colour.

rows.name: periodicity_test.sh
rows.what_it_does: The half-tile test: bakes a recipe, bakes it again slid by half a tile, compares, with a wrong-roll control.
rows.evidence: Reading; the slate layers' own `tests/half_tile_layers.py` is the fuller version (below).

rows.kind: 4C. The slate made of separate layers (`recipes/slate_layers/`; the trials import the layer files from the frozen snapshot)
rows.what_it_does: The fixed contract: the eleven bundle numbers, the four outputs of every layer, sizes in tile units, seamless rules, declared links, setting names.
rows.evidence: The brick reuse ran on it unchanged; look check today; no shared layer reads `row`.
rows.wood: as is, with the bundle turned (`local_y` along the grain)

rows.name: layers/layer_interface.py

rows.name: layers/layout.py (the slate LAYOUT)
rows.kind: 4C. The slate made of separate layers (`recipes/slate_layers/`; the trials import the layer files from the frozen snapshot)
rows.what_it_does: Makes rows of pieces with random widths, leaning joints, rounded and chipped edges, and hands out the bundle.
rows.evidence: Range check today: values above a control's listed range are kept.
rows.brick: settings only: 12 rows of 4, joint 0.016, row gap 0.0148 (not baked yet)
rows.wood: settings only: 5 rows of 1 piece, plus the 10-node turn in the recipe (not baked yet)

rows.name: layers/colour_and_fade.py
rows.kind: 4C. The slate made of separate layers (`recipes/slate_layers/`; the trials import the layer files from the frozen snapshot)
rows.what_it_does: The bottom paint: a tone per piece, tongues and tall mottling patches on the piece's own coordinates, specks, big bleached and damp patches across pieces, palette rounding for flat paint.
rows.evidence: Look check sheet; reading the code.
rows.brick: settings only: the three tongue-removing settings (look check)
rows.wood: settings only, on the turned bundle (look check)
rows.metal: settings only: steel blue-greys, patches 1.45 times taller than wide (not tried)
rows.mud: settings only: one earth tone per clod plus dry and wet areas (not tried)
rows.gravel: settings only: one tone per stone; `fade_direction` -1 = lit from the top (not tried)

rows.name: layers/damage.py
rows.kind: 4C. The slate made of separate layers (`recipes/slate_layers/`; the trials import the layer files from the frozen snapshot)
rows.what_it_does: Flakes along edges (mostly the lower edge and corners), pits, scratches, cracks from an edge, bites, broken corners; sinks the relief.
rows.evidence: Look check zoom; reading. Confined to pieces.
rows.brick: settings only: pale sandy chips at edges and corners (brick reuse, look check)
rows.wood: needs code changes: its cracks always start at a piece edge (on turned boards: at the board end, look check), wood cracks start anywhere along the grain; or a new CRACKS layer. Chips: settings only
rows.metal: settings only: chipped paint at bar edges in bare-steel colours, rust pits, two long scratches (not tried)
rows.mud: settings only: dark crumbly rims on clod edges (not tried, unsure)
rows.gravel: settings only: pale flakes at stone edges, pits as rust spots (not tried)

rows.name: layers/moss.py
rows.kind: 4C. The slate made of separate layers (`recipes/slate_layers/`; the trials import the layer files from the frozen snapshot)
rows.what_it_does: Growth: flat clumps gathered by rules (drips from the upper edge, joints, lower part, low spots, a big patch gate) and round lichen discs in colonies; can avoid or seek damage.
rows.evidence: Reading: confined to pieces; its clump noise is read on piece coordinates.
rows.brick: settings only: little or none (the brick reference shows no moss); if kept, change its olive tones (teal on red in the look check)
rows.wood: settings only: moss off; lichen discs in rust browns = the rust splatter (look check: they appear, too few)
rows.metal: settings only, as RUST: drips down from upper edges, along bar edges, clumped by panel, `damage_attract` = rust in chipped paint (not tried)
rows.mud: settings only, unsure: as puddle WATER (rules off, big gate on), lichen discs as small stones; may need a new PUDDLES layer
rows.gravel: settings only: off, or a few rust spots

rows.name: layers/outline_and_shadow.py
rows.kind: 4C. The slate made of separate layers (`recipes/slate_layers/`; the trials import the layer files from the frozen snapshot)
rows.what_it_does: The drawing: dark gaps, thin side outline, stepped shadow band under each piece's upper edge, pale lip on its lower edge, edge darkening; small relief.
rows.evidence: Brick reuse sheet; look check; reading: the shadow and lip belong to each piece's own upper and lower edge.
rows.brick: settings only: gap = mortar colour, thin dark ring, the lip used as a DARK lower rim; the mortar stays flat (texture comes from GRIME)
rows.wood: settings only: dark gaps, thin outline, no shadow band, no lip (look check)
rows.metal: settings only for half: creases and the shadow under horizontal bars; the bright upper-left edge and the shadow right of vertical bars need EDGE LIGHT
rows.mud: not useful: mud has no joints (Amount 0, or a 1-dot crack between clods)
rows.gravel: settings only: gap colour = soil base colour, thin rim, no shadow band, no lip (stones have no dark outline)
